title: The end-point's own conversation token beside the peer's, in one exchange

provenance.quote: A NLIP message may contain multiple submessages with format fields of 'token'. As an example, in a communication, each of the end-points may include their own 'conversation' token and 'authentication' token that they have created, resulting in two submessages per end-point with the format field of 'token' in the message.

notes: §6.2 ¶3's "two submessages per end-point" arrangement, with the two rules that govern it pulling in opposite directions on the same message. `srv-1` is withheld by §6.2's exception and restored by §6.2.1's confirmation, once; `cli-1` is the peer's and comes straight back; and nothing is minted, because the peer already named the conversation. An implementation that answered "did the peer bring a conversation token?" with one question rather than two gets this case wrong in one of two ways — either it mints `srv-new` beside `srv-1`, or it counts `srv-1` as the peer's and drops the confirmation.
